title: Engineer 3-minute technical snack deck (quick pitch for platform/infra)
content:
Slide 1 — 3-min opener: what you can say in 30s
- One-liner: 'We make inference predictable and cheap to run in production — whether you keep it hosted or run it in your VPC.'
- Why engineers care: predictable p99 latency, rollouts that don’t break caches, and clear cost levers (batching/quantization/routing).
- Quick ask: 'Can I show you a 5-request demo and a simple SLA we can hit in your region?'

Slide 2 — Quick architecture sketch (30s talking points)
- Two halves: Redwood control plane + customer runtime (hosted, dedicated, or private).
- Path: SDK -> routing -> runtime -> GPU/quantized model -> KV cache -> client streaming.
- Callout: same API surface across modes — demos and tests are portable.
- Speaker tip: emphasize 'same code paths you write now work across all modes' to reduce friction for infra teams.

Slide 3 — Measurable claims (keep concrete)
- Typical p50/p90/p99 from our public benchmarks: 12ms/36ms/120ms token-step on xG-series (quantized late-binding, continuous batching). (Use only as example; refer to perf repo for region-specific numbers.)
- Average token-cost delta when enabling smart batching + cache: 30–60% reduction on chat workloads.
- Demonstration line: 'We can show you p99 target in 10 minutes using a 5-user synthetic traffic profile.'

Slide 4 — Top technical objections and one-liners (30s)
- 'I can self-host cheaper.' -> 'Maybe — but we reduce engineering ops and ramp risk: autoscaling policies + rollout controls cut incidents during canaries.'
- 'Latency spikes under load.' -> 'We have adaptive batching and priority lanes that preserve tail latency for critical routes.'
- 'Data residency/compliance.' -> 'Private deployments: customer-managed VPC with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs.'

Slide 5 — Quick demo plan (what to run in 5–10 minutes)
- Step 0 (pre-demo): request a small sample prompt set and target p99 SLA (e.g., 350ms token-step).
- Step 1: SDK quickstart (JS/py) to send 5 concurrent chat requests (copy-paste snippet).
- Step 2: Flip routing to a dedicated pool and compare p99 + token costs in console.
- Step 3: Show a canary rollback: change model variant, auto-fallback to cheaper quantized variant during induced load spike.
- Win condition: customer sees measurable p99 and cost delta within the demo timeframe.

Slide 6 — Minimal commands / snippets to include in speak notes
- Python SDK snippet (one-liner example): from redwood import Client; c = Client(api_key=...); c.chat.create(model='rwd-compact-1', messages=[...])
- CLI: redwood profile set --region=us-west1; redwood run demo-workload --concurrency=5 --duration=30s
- Tip: keep both JS and Python paste-ready in a single note so SEs can pick language.

Slide 7 — Negotiation playbook for platform teams (fast checks)
- Ask 1: 'What’s your p99 and target SLA for interactive routes?' (if target < 500ms, propose dedicated or edge-region.)
- Ask 2: 'Are you optimizing for throughput (batch) or latency (priority lanes)?'
- Security check: 'Do you need customer-managed KMS or on-prem packaging?'
- Pricing play: propose short-term dedicated trial credit with a rollback to hosted if volume isn’t met.

Slide 8 — Mini FAQ (answers you should memorize)
- Q: 'How do you guarantee no model drift?' A: 'Model pinning + rollout windows + automatic rollback on eval regressions.'
- Q: 'What if my token costs balloon?' A: 'We monitor token economics and recommend quantization or cache policies; we can run a cost-savings simulation on your prompt set.'
- Q: 'How do we debug tail latency?' A: 'Tracing hooks per request, token-level timing in console, and trace export to your observability stack.'

Slide 9 — Tactical follow-up checklist (post-call)
- Send 1-pager with three tailored numbers: expected p99, demo checklist, and estimated committed spend for dedicated tier.
- Attach a short runbook for the technical trial (1–2 commands, credentials, contact for escalation).
- Offer up a 2-hour joint run to iterate on prompts and caching rules.

Slide 10 — Closing one-liner & CTA (keep short)
- One-liner to drop at the end: 'We let you control the economics and the SLA — we do the heavy lifting so your infra team can move faster.'
- CTA: 'Can we schedule a 2-hour live trial next week? I'll bring a runbook and a small cost-savings projection for your sample prompts.'

Appendix — Quick rebut scripts (very short)
- If buyer says 'we tried caching before, it didn't help' -> 'Caching is only effective if we align cache keys with user session prefixes; we can test a prefix-based policy on your dataset in 30 mins.'
- If buyer asks about vendor lock-in -> 'Same API and model pinning means you can export traces and runbooks; dedicated contracts include an exit checklist.'

Notes to self (rough)
- Keep slide count small for an SE: 8–10 slides max. Use speaker notes heavily.
- For demo, prepare a synthetic 20-user profile and a single 500-token average prompt to stress test batching.
- Cross-check public perf matrix before the call and swap numbers to match the customer's hardware/region.

Unresolved / TODOs
- Add precise region-specific p99 numbers (reach out to infra for last week's perf run).
- Attach ready-to-paste SDK snippets for Go and Java (priority: py/js first).
- Get approval from legal on the demo trial credit language (billing exposure).

End of snack deck (very rough)
- This is intentionally terse and conversational; meant for SEs/AE technical touches to use live.
